intent: A firewall apply (setup_wireguard_ssh.sh allow-*) no longer bounces Docker and its containers, and the DoT rule (tcp/853 on wg0) survives every re-apply instead of vanishing.
scope: linux_configuration/features/lib/wg_firewall.sh: ruleset replaces only 'table inet filter'; restore_docker_rules restarts docker only when its nat DOCKER chain is gone; ALLOW_DOT renders 853 on wg0; allow_dot()
linux_configuration/features/setup_wireguard_ssh.sh, lib/wg_sshd.sh: ALLOW_DOT default/save_config, allow-dot subcommand and usage
linux_configuration/features/lib/dot_resolver_install.sh: wg-bound branch goes through 'setup_wireguard_ssh.sh allow-dot' instead of a runtime 'nft add rule'
Tests: new lib/tests/test_wg_firewall.sh; test_dot_resolver_install.sh wg-branch cases rewritten
Non-goal: the publicly bound DoT branch still adds its rate-limited rule at runtime
changes: 'flush ruleset' replaced by 'table inet filter' + 'delete table inet filter' before the definition: atomic, leaves Docker's (iptables-nft) and Tailscale's tables alone, and loads on a first boot
restore_docker_rules checks 'iptables -t nat -S DOCKER' and only restarts docker when that chain is missing
sshd-death rollback deletes only inet filter instead of flushing the whole ruleset
ALLOW_DOT persisted in .wireguard_ssh.conf; open_firewall calls allow-dot so the rule is rendered on every apply

verification.command: vmbox guest dotfw (iptables-nft, docker 29 + busybox probe, an extra 'inet sentinel' table): old HEAD allow-homeassistant vs new allow-dot
verification.evidence: old: all non-inet-filter tables deleted, docker + probe restarted; new re-apply from healthy state: docker ActiveEnterTimestamp and probe StartedAt unchanged, sentinel and docker tables kept; verify clean; systemctl restart nftables and first-boot load (no table) rc=0

'docker's own firewall rules are intact; containers untouched'; docker since 2026-09-28 12:41:15 and gitea-caddy StartedAt unchanged; live input chain gains iifname wg0 tcp dport 853 accept; verify: nftables.conf matches; anki/gitea HTTPS 200
12 passed incl. real nft -c; jailed suite rc=0

risks: Tables left over from an older ruleset outside inet filter are no longer flushed by an apply (none exist on the host).
If docker's rules live somewhere other than the nat DOCKER chain, a missing-rules state would not trigger the rebuild.
rollback: git revert this commit, then sudo setup_wireguard_ssh.sh allow-web to re-render (old code restarts docker once)
After rollback: setup_wireguard_ssh.sh verify, and confirm containers reach the network
